answer: Entry-bond vaults resist Sybil attacks: every new agent must lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can trade, and each stake is anchored to a single verifiable work history that cannot be split across aliases. A public lantern ledger publishes each identity's past performance, so a swarm of fresh, history-less fakes glows suspiciously bright and peers simply refuse them. An attacker must fund and age each fake separately; honest agents pay once and earn the bond back, while a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds plus months of waiting.
